_doc: Sanitizer rule-spec — the ONE machine-readable source of truth for the
content rules shared by the Go DB sanitizer (internal/core/sanitize.go,
which embeds this file) and the Python harvest sanitizer
(scripts/harvest_fixtures.py, which reads it from the repo).
Neither implementation may carry its own copy of these tables.
The two implementations deliberately DIFFER beyond these rules: the
harvest script additionally pseudonymizes ids, aliases project paths and
salts the placeholder hash, because its output is published as committed
fixtures; the DB sanitizer keeps ids and paths verbatim with an unsalted
hash, because the DB is local-first. Those harvest-only behaviors use
Contract vectors live in testdata/sanitizer-vectors/; both
implementations must produce byte-identical output over them
content_keys_doc: values that are content by definition — always stripped to a placeholder, any length, any type (an entire tool_use input object becomes one placeholder). Includes short content-bearing fields found in real logs that slip under the max_free_len rule (aiTitle, lastPrompt, subject, description).
string_content_keys_doc: keys whose STRING values are stripped but whose list/dict values keep their structure and are recursed into (the message.content block array).
safe_keys_doc: keys whose string values are known-safe metadata at any length (ids, timestamps, models, ...). The harvest sanitizer still pseudonymizes id-shaped and aliases path-shaped values regardless of this list.
max_free_len_doc: unknown string fields longer than this many UTF-8 BYTES are stripped; at or under it they pass through (a pure length threshold is not a content filter — newly observed free-text keys go into content_keys).

placeholder.doc: the stripped-content marker. len = UTF-8 byte length of the hashed input; hash = first hash_hex_chars lowercase hex chars of sha256(salt_utf8 + input_utf8). The DB sanitizer uses an empty salt; the harvest sanitizer salts per harvest. Non-string values are first encoded per nonstring_encoding; strings hash their raw UTF-8 bytes.
placeholder.nonstring_encoding: canonical JSON: object keys sorted, compact separators (',' ':'), non-ASCII unescaped (raw UTF-8), no HTML escaping
placeholder.idempotency: a string already matching regex passes through every sanitizer verbatim, even under content keys

id_shapes.doc: string shapes treated as opaque identifiers: kept verbatim by the DB sanitizer, pseudonymized shape-preservingly by the harvest sanitizer.

pathlike_doc: a string is path-shaped when it starts with '/' or '~', or starts with '.' and contains '/', or contains '/' and no whitespace. Path-shaped values pass through the DB sanitizer verbatim and are aliased segment-wise by the harvest sanitizer.

harvest.doc: tables used only by the harvest sanitizer's aliasing layer (committed-fixture publication); the DB sanitizer ignores this section.
harvest.path_keyed_maps_doc: maps whose keys are file paths BY SCHEMA: every key is tokenized to p-<8hex>[.ext] unconditionally — no path-likeness heuristics (extensionless keys like 'Makefile' must not slip through). The leak checker enforces the same set on committed fixtures.
harvest.git_branch_allowlist_doc: gitBranch values kept verbatim; everything else becomes branch-<6hex>.
harvest.path_segment_allowlist_doc: structural path segments carrying no project identity, kept verbatim BEFORE the project segment only; every segment after the project segment becomes a sanitizer token.
